key_insight: STRIDE uses a large language model to refine noisy sepsis labels from EHRs, improving detection accuracy across multiple hospitals.
clinical_relevance: Better label quality can support more reliable sepsis surveillance and reduce unnecessary alerts in clinical workflows.
method: Applied an LLM to discharge summaries to refine a pragmatic sepsis definition.
Trained and tested models with 8-, 24-, and 48-hour observation windows across seven hospitals.
Benchmarked performance against SOFA, SIRS, and Epic, with physician-adjudicated cases as the gold standard.
evidence_signal: In 356,610 encounters, the 8-hour model reached AUC 0.960 in derivation and 0.878 in physician-adjudicated validation, with favorable calibration and 78.2% specificity at 80% sensitivity.
watch_item: Performance should be validated for local workflows because label refinement and alert utility may vary by hospital setting and documentation practices.
paper_title: Language model-assisted label refinement for accurate sepsis detection from electronic health records
